account_number.description: Brokerage account number; pass to any tool that requires account_number. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number — pass this (not account_number) to any nummus-backed tool that asks for an account identifier.

rhc_account_number.description: Crypto account number for this account (e.g. 'RHC1234567'). Absent when no linked crypto account exists. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

type.description: 'cash', 'margin', or 'limited_margin' — the trading-permissions classification for the brokerage account. 'limited_margin' (instant settlement without full margin leverage) applies to accounts where full margin is unavailable, such as retirement (IRA), managed, and agentic accounts. Crypto accounts are never marginable, so a linked crypto account has no equivalent.

unsettled_funds.description: Proceeds from recent sales not yet settled (cash accounts settle T+1), in the account's currency. Informational only and may lag live trading — this is NOT a spendable or order-gating figure; buying_power from get_portfolio is authoritative for what can be traded now. A cash-type account with unsettled_funds greater than 0 could trade with those proceeds immediately by upgrading to limited margin. Absent when upstream does not report it — treat as unknown, not zero.

nickname.description: User-set nickname; present alongside account_number when set. Cosmetic only — not an agentic_allowed or agentic-account signal.

is_default.description: True for the user's default account. Surface when choosing among multiple accounts.

agentic_allowed.description: True when this account is accessible to this agent specifically. An account with false may be agentic-enabled but scoped to a different agent type — do not tell the user it is disabled. Sole source of truth for eligibility — never infer it from nickname text. review_*/place_*/cancel_* tools reject accounts where this is false.

option_level.description: Options approval: 'option_level_2' (long calls/puts, covered calls, cash-secured puts), 'option_level_3' (spreads and complex strategies), or empty/'option_level_0' (not approved).

user_option_level.description: The caller's own options approval on a multi-member (trust) account: 'option_level_2', 'option_level_3', or absent. Absent on single-owner and joint accounts and whenever the caller holds no level of their own. When present and below option_level the caller is view-only for options on this account and cannot place, replace, cancel or exercise; treat user_option_level, not option_level, as their tradable level.

management_type.description: Management classification (e.g. 'managed') when applicable; layered on top of brokerage_account_type rather than replacing it.

affiliate.description: Affiliate / region code (e.g. 'RHF', 'RHUK', 'RHSG'). Affects feature availability for the account.

state.description: Account state — 'active' is normal; anything else (deactivated, restricted, etc.) means the account cannot trade normally.

deactivated.description: True when the account is currently deactivated.

permanently_deactivated.description: True when the account is permanently closed (cannot be reactivated).

accounts.description: The user's brokerage accounts. Empty when the user has none.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Sort the list deterministically when presenting: the default account first, agentic accounts (agentic_allowed=true) second, then other individual accounts, then retirement (IRA) accounts. Present account_number, rhc_account_number (label it "Crypto Account"), brokerage_account_type (label it "Account Type" — a linked crypto account always shares it, so never add a separate crypto account type column), type (label it "Brokerage Trading Type"), nickname (if set), and is_default — in that column order. In the Crypto Account column show "N/A" for accounts with an empty rhc_account_number; omit the column entirely only when no account has one. When referring to the account in user-facing prose (e.g. "your <X> account"), use nickname when set; fall back to brokerage_account_type otherwise. When displaying account_number or rhc_account_number to the user, mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234'); pass the full value to other tools unchanged — including get_option_level_upgrade_info and any fallback upgrade URL; masking breaks the link. Flag agentic_allowed when the user is choosing an account for a trade. There is exactly one agentic_allowed=true account — use it directly rather than asking which account to trade. agentic_allowed is caller-relative — true means accessible to this agent, false means this agent cannot act on it (the account may still be agentic-enabled for a different agent). Never state agentic_allowed's field name or raw boolean value to the user. Do not use nickname to determine agentic-account eligibility. Skip false accounts for trade operations; if the user asks why, say the account is not accessible to this agent, not that it needs to be enabled. When user_option_level is present (multi-member trust accounts), it is this user's own options level on that account and is the level to reason about for options actions there; if it is below option_level the user is view-only for options on that account. When user_option_level is absent on a trust account (brokerage_account_type='trust_revocable'), the user holds no options level of their own there — do not offer options actions on that account, even though option_level is set. When option_level is empty or 'option_level_0' and the user wants options, call get_option_level_upgrade_info with the account_number; if that tool is unavailable, direct the user to https://applink.robinhood.com/upgrade_options?account_number=<that account's account_number> (embed the full unmasked account_number in the URL). management_type='managed' is layered on brokerage_account_type — surface alongside, not as a replacement. For tools that ask for an account identifier on a crypto-backed flow (get_crypto_positions, future crypto write tools), pass rhs_account_number; for everything else (equities, options, etc.) pass account_number. Do not add an unsettled_funds column to the account table — surface it only via the following rule. Whenever you report an account's funds, value, or buying power and that account has type='cash' with unsettled_funds greater than 0, and the user wants to access unsettled funds or other features available in a limited margin account — if the get_limited_margin_upgrade_info tool is available — call it with the account_number and share the appropriate upgrade link. If that tool is not available, say nothing about limited margin (there is no fallback).

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Obtain from get_accounts.

total_value.description: Total portfolio value across all asset types. The default 'account value' to show the user.

equity_value.description: Value of stock and ETF positions.

futures_value.description: Value of futures positions (includes RHD cost basis).

cash.description: Available cash (includes early access from pending deposits).

pending_deposits.description: Deposits in transit, not yet settled.

currency.description: Currency all values are denominated in (e.g. USD).

buying_power.description: Authoritative spendable figure used to gate order placement. For margin-enabled accounts it already includes available margin leverage; for cash and leverage-disabled accounts it equals the cash-only figure.

unleveraged_buying_power.description: Buying power ignoring margin leverage. Typically <= buying_power. Negative when the account is in deficit — new positions cannot be opened until the deficit is cleared.

intraday_buying_power.description: Buying power for intraday leverage, when applicable; null when the account does not have intraday margin enabled.

off_intraday_buying_power.description: Buying power outside the intraday-leverage window; null when not applicable.

buying_power.description: Real-time buying power from the broker.
Authoritative spendable figure for crypto buys (cash-only; excludes equity margin leverage).

crypto_buying_power.description: Spendable buying power for crypto buys. Cash-only (crypto is not marginable), so it excludes the equity margin leverage that buying_power may include — quote this for 'how much can I spend on crypto'. Omitted when unavailable.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Show total_value as "account value" or "portfolio value". The breakdown fields show how value is distributed across asset types. Zero-value fields mean the user has no holdings in that asset class — omit them from display unless the user explicitly asks. For "how much cash do I have?" use the cash field. buying_power is the real-time authoritative spendable figure from the broker; quote buying_power.buying_power as the primary affordability answer with buying_power.display_currency. For "how much can I spend on crypto?" quote crypto_buying_power.buying_power instead — crypto is cash-only (not marginable), so the top-level buying_power may overstate it; crypto_buying_power is omitted when unavailable. crypto_value reflects the user's crypto holdings value. On a cash account, recently sold proceeds that have not yet settled are not spendable and are not included in buying_power; that unsettled amount is reported as unsettled_funds by get_accounts (not here), so if you do not already have the account's unsettled_funds, call get_accounts to check it. Whenever you report buying power or account value for a type='cash' account whose unsettled_funds is greater than 0, and the user wants to access unsettled funds or other features available in a limited margin account — if the get_limited_margin_upgrade_info tool is available — call it with the account_number and share the appropriate upgrade link. If that tool is not available, say nothing about limited margin (there is no fallback).
